> **TL;DR**: What does the file structure of an AI agent system actually look like? This git-tree-style visualization reveals the directory layout, skill organization, and evolution tracking behind a production agent setup.

## Quick Summary

- Skills live in a flat directory structure under `~/.config/opencode/skills/`
- Each skill follows an identical skeleton: SKILL.md, context/, templates/, history/
- Trigger words map to skill directories via `triggers.yaml`
- Meta-skills like `skill-factory` can create and evolve other skills
- Retired skills move to `_archive/` rather than being deleted

## The Tree Structure

If you `tree` the configuration directory of an AI agent system, you get something surprisingly readable. Every skill has the same structure. Every directory has a purpose. Here's what it looks like:

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Skill Tree View" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;margin:1.5rem auto;border-radius:8px;" />

## Anatomy of a Skill Directory

Every skill follows the same skeleton. This consistency is deliberate — it means any model, even a 7B parameter one, can navigate and execute skills correctly without special casing.

### SKILL.md — The Core

The `SKILL.md` file is the skill's brain. It uses progressive disclosure with levels:

| Level | Content | When Loaded |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| L0 | Trigger, one-line description | Always |
| L1 | Capabilities, quick reference | On skill match |
| L2 | Full workflow, examples | During execution |
| L3 | Edge cases, troubleshooting | On error/retry |
| L4 | Full API reference, history | Deep debugging |

A skill like `astro` has 7 levels because blog publishing has complex failure modes. A simpler skill like `svg` has 4. The system loads only what's needed.

### context/ — Metadata Layer

The `context/` directory holds `intent.md` (what the skill is for) and `metadata.json` (version, dependencies, tags). This separation means the agent can check compatibility without loading the full skill.

### templates/ — Reusable Output

HTML wrappers, email templates, document scaffolds — anything the skill generates goes here. The `svg` skill keeps its HTML wrapper template here so diagrams can be previewed in a browser instantly.

### history/ — Evolution Log

Every skill tracks its own evolution. The `history/sessions/` directory contains dated session logs documenting what changed and why. This is the skill's git history — a self-documenting audit trail.

## The Trigger System

Triggers in `triggers.yaml` are the routing layer. They're validated by a Python script that ensures:

1. No duplicate triggers exist across skills
2. Every trigger maps to a skill directory that exists
3. No orphaned skills without trigger entries

The validation runs as a pre-commit check, preventing broken trigger resolution from reaching production.

## Meta-Skills: Skills That Create Skills

The `skill-factory/` directory is a meta-skill — a skill whose purpose is creating other skills. It reads a specification, generates the directory skeleton, writes SKILL.md with progressive disclosure scaffolding, and creates the history log.

This is the recursive principle in action: the system contains the tools to extend itself.

## Archive, Don't Delete

Retired skills move to `_archive/` with a timestamp suffix. This preserves history and allows resurrection. The archival prohibition policy (documented in AGENTS.md) ensures no skill is moved without explicit per-skill user confirmation.

<details>
<summary>Technical Details: Directory Skeleton Generator</summary>

The skill-factory generates this structure for every new skill:

```
new-skill/
├── SKILL.md          # Progressive disclosure content
├── skill.yaml        # Machine-readable metadata
├── context/
│   ├── intent.md     # Purpose and scope
│   └── metadata.json # Version, deps, tags
├── templates/        # Output templates
├── scripts/          # Automation scripts
└── history/
    ├── changes.log   # Changelog
    └── sessions/     # Session logs
```

Every directory is created even if empty — the consistent structure is the contract.

</details>
